description: When several pull requests merge into main back to back, every push to main runs the full unit and stress suites even though each pushed tree is a subset of the next one. On 2026-11-26 four merges in 80 seconds started three full CI sets within 2 minutes (macOS unit 292 s, 425 s and more, survival 291, 269 and 207 s, ubuntu unit 156, 122 and 162 s), about 25 runner-minutes for trees that each contain the previous one. scripts/ci_main_push_gate.py (decide_main_push) only skips a push whose pull request head already ran the same tree; for a burst the pushed tree never equals the head tree (rule main-push-tree-mismatch), so nothing is skipped. Measured saving: about 17 runner-minutes per extra merge in a burst.
goal: A push to main whose commit is no longer the tip of main when the gate job starts, and whose commit is an ancestor of that tip, records a skip with the new rule main-push-superseded (detail naming the pushed sha and the tip sha) and relies on the newest tip's run, which tests a superset tree. Only the tip of a burst runs the full suite. Any doubt (the tip cannot be read, the pushed commit is not an ancestor of the tip, the run is a re-run attempt, an API error) keeps the existing behaviour, a full run. The existing rules, including main-push-tested-tree, are unchanged for the tip commit. The new check lives in a small new module under scripts/ so ci_main_push_gate.py stays well under its module budget, and the decision log line and workflow summary name the rule so the saving can be counted. The daily scheduled full run is untouched.
rationale: A burst of N merges should cost one full CI run instead of N; attribution of a red tip is covered because every pull request head was already green on its own base.
acceptance_criteria: decide_main_push in scripts/ci_main_push_gate.py returns a skip with rule main-push-superseded, computed in the new scripts/ci_main_push_superseded.py, when the pushed commit is an ancestor of, and not equal to, the current tip of main; a test in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_ci_main_push_superseded.py asserts it with the fake gate client.

It returns a full run, keeping the earlier rules unchanged, when the pushed commit is the tip, when the pushed commit is not an ancestor of the tip, when the tip lookup raises, and on a re-run attempt; one test each. The existing apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_ci_main_push_gate.py, test_ci_bookkeeping_wiring.py and test_ci_merge_push_gate.py still pass.
The superseded check adds at most two API reads per gated job and none when the pushed commit is the tip beyond the tip read itself.

No module line budget is raised and holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json is unchanged; scripts/ci_main_push_gate.py, scripts/ci_bookkeeping_api.py, scripts/ci_bookkeeping_chain.py, scripts/ci_bookkeeping_gate.py and scripts/ci_merge_push_gate.py keep working with their existing tests (test_ci_bookkeeping_gate.py, test_ci_bookkeeping_chain.py).
'uv run pytest' on the changed and added tests, 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.
